descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. About the Team The Global Resource Management team is a small, focused group of engineers dedicated to driving organization and clarity across Cloudflare's platform. We develop and maintain applications that live in the foundational platform to enable features that span all of Cloudflare’s resources. The work we do is absolutely critical to enabling Cloudflare to scale its operations efficiently, reach new customers, and maintain the reliability our users expect. Joining us means working on the core of Cloudflare's ability to operate and grow. What You’ll Do As a System Engineer on the Global Resource Management team, you'll be at the forefront of tackling our most challenging system architecture problems: Solve Deep, Foundational Problems: Dive into complex, cross-cutting engineering challenges that benefit all Cloudflare products by creating organized, efficient, and well-managed applications. Architect for Organization and Clarity: Design and make core architectural decisions focused on reducing fanout and simplifying system dependencies. The objective is to make platform adoption seamless and straightforward for product engineering teams. Build Scalable Systems: Be responsible for proposing architectures, writing detailed specifications, and implementing high-quality, maintainable code to build scalable and highly available systems. Drive Code Quality: Actively participate in thorough code reviews, provide constructive feedback on technical specifications and designs, and ensure all implementations adhere to best practices for reliability and security. Skills, Knowledge, and Experience Professional Experience: 5+ years of professional experience in software development, building and operating mission-critical, high-scale distributed systems. Programming Languages: Strong proficiency in Go (Golang) or a similar modern systems language. Systems Design: Proven experience in designing, building, and operating scalable, highly available services at cloud-scale. Architectural Thinking: Understanding of concepts related to organization, dependency management, and resource orchestration in a large, multi-tenant environment. Collaboration: Experience participating in a code review process and contributing thoughtful feedback to design specifications. Comfortable working across teams to identify shared challenges and propose platform-level solutions. Bonus Skills: Familiarity with Cloudflare's core technologies, such as edge computing or global networking. Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools and related technologies.   Compensation Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location. Equity This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity We are looking for a Senior Director of Corporate FP&A to join Grafana Labs and help build and scale our Corporate FP&A function as the company enters its next phase of growth. This is a pivotal leadership role responsible for building the financial infrastructure and operating cadence that power company-wide planning, forecasting, reporting, and decision-making. You will own key Corporate FP&A processes, including long-range planning, annual planning, consolidated P&L, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow forecasting, executive and Board reporting, while helping establish the rigor, systems, and insights required to support the company’s next phase of growth. You will serve as a key partner to Finance, business leaders, and the executive leadership team, translating operating performance into clear financial insights and helping drive fast, informed decisions. The ideal candidate is a seasoned, results-oriented finance leader with strong business judgment, high integrity, and a track record of building scalable processes in complex, high-growth environments. You should be equally comfortable operating strategically and going deep into the details, with the ability to identify what needs to be built and raise the overall standard of Corporate FP&A. This is an opportunity to build the foundation for Corporate FP&A at a high-growth global company. The role is fully remote and will report to the VP of Finance. What you'll be doing: Own the company-wide Corporate FP&A model and planning processes, including long-range planning, annual planning, monthly forecasting, and consolidated P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow forecasting. Lead executive and Board reporting, delivering clear, decision-ready materials and commentary on business performance, key drivers, risks, opportunities, and operating leverage. Build and continuously refine the company’s KPI and reporting architecture, including scorecards, dashboards, recurring business reviews, and analytical frameworks that leadership and investors can rely on. Partner closely with Accounting, Tax, and other Finance teams to support month-end close, flux reviews, and financial reporting. Establish and continuously improve Corporate FP&A operating rhythms, including close-to-insight timelines, clear ownership, metric definitions, and reporting processes designed to support the company’s next phase of growth. Lead the modernization of Finance processes, forecasting methodologies, and planning frameworks through systems, workflow automation, structured data, and AI to improve accuracy, scalability, and the quality of forward-looking insights as the business evolves. Build strong cross-functional relationships with business and functional leaders, serving as a trusted partner on financial performance, resource allocation, and strategic decision-making. Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing Corporate FP&A team, and support strategic initiatives such as M&A diligence and integration as needed. What Makes You a Great Fit: 10+ years of experience across FP&A, Strategic Finance, Corporate Finance, or related disciplines, including meaningful experience at a leading technology company and ideally complementary experience in investment banking or buy-side investing. Experience in SaaS, enterprise software, or the broader technology sector is strongly preferred. Corporate FP&A leadership experience, ideally in a public-company, newly public, or public-company-readiness environment, with exposure to quarterly close, executive reporting, Board reporting, and other rigorous financial operating cadences. Meaningful experience owning a consolidated P&L, company-wide forecast, and Balance Sheet and Cash Flow forecasting processes. Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills, with the ability to build models from scratch, pressure-test assumptions, identify root causes, and translate complex analysis into clear, actionable insights. Strong executive presence and communication skills, with experience preparing and presenting decision-ready materials to senior leadership and the Board, and influencing significant company decisions. Proven ability to serve as a trusted business partner across functions and geographies, with strong business judgment and a track record of building effective cross-functional relationships. Demonstrated success as a change agent, improving forecasting, planning, reporting, and operating processes as organizations scale. What you’ll do here Coordinate virtual and in-person interviews across teams and time zones, ensuring a smooth experience for everyone involved Thoroughly document interview processes, interviewer roles, and other relevant details to help better prepare candidates and interviewers Proactively identify opportunities to streamline coordination and improve the candidate and hiring team experience Generally support day-to-day recruiting operations What we’re looking for 1+ year(s) of experience in recruiting coordination, talent acquisition, HR, administrative support, or another similar role Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to juggle competing priorities Clear and friendly communication, both written and verbal A candidate-first mindset and genuine interest in creating a positive experience for everyone involved in hiring Experience using AI, an Applicant Tracking System (Ashby, Greenhouse, etc.), and standard web-based tools (Google Workspace or similar) Bonus tacos if you have (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!) Experience using Ashby ATS Prior experience at a quickly scaling technical startup Interest in growing professionally into a full-cycle Recruiter About Coder Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com . We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow. Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a Senior Product Manager for Data Integrations, you'll help GitLab's analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) agents see beyond the data held in GitLab. You'll decide which external systems connect to the Data Insights Platform and Orbit, which integrations come first, and how their data fits into shared models. Engineering teams plan work, track incidents, monitor production, and manage security findings across different tools. Your challenge is to bring that context together with GitLab's code, merge requests, pipelines, deployments, and vulnerabilities. You'll shape a consistent approach that gives customers a trustworthy picture they can query, report on, and use with agents, rather than another set of disconnected data sources. This role is based in Bangalore, India. You'll work from home and come to the Bangalore office when needed for business or team activities. You should be based in Bangalore or willing to relocate there. What you'll do Set integration priorities using evidence from customers, field teams, and other product managers to identify the biggest gaps in context. Shape how external data maps into GitLab's shared data models, including the extract, transform, and load (ETL) approach and the transformations needed to make sources work together. Define the customer problems and user groups each integration serves. Partner with engineering to agree on the intended experience, trade-offs, and delivery sequence. Translate product decisions into a clear backlog of epics and issues for engineering. Define telemetry and adoption signals to understand whether connected data helps customers answer new questions, and use those findings to guide priorities. Help shape integration pricing and packaging as the product area matures. Use AI coding agents and GitLab to explore data, prototype integrations, and document the intended experience. What you'll bring Product management experience, with the ability to connect customer needs to priorities and make trade-offs with incomplete information. Strong knowledge of the software development and operations (DevOps) ecosystem, including how planning, security, observability, and IT service management tools fit into engineering workflows. A working understanding of data integration, ETL, and data transformation, including how data from different systems maps to a common model. You don't need a background as a data engineer. Comfort using AI tools for prototyping and documentation as part of your product work. Clear communication about customer problems, close collaboration with engineering, and a habit of using data to evaluate adoption. Experience with integration products, data models, or value stream analytics is helpful, but isn't required. About the team We're part of GitLab's Core Data Products organization, which focuses on insights, analytics, and data-driven decision-making. You'll report to the Vice President of Product Management and join as our third product manager, focused on Data Integrations. You'll work alongside a Principal Product Manager responsible for the Data Insights Platform and dashboards, and a Product Manager focused on Orbit. GitLab is all-remote, with asynchronous collaboration across regions. Transparency, written communication, and clear decisions are central to how we work. This role has the Bangalore location and in-person requirements described above. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity: We are looking for a results driven leader to manage and grow our US Sales Development team and help us expand our business in the region. Reporting to the Director of NORAM Sales Development, you will be an important contributor to our regional leadership team, driving recruiting, pipeline generation strategy, and proactive coaching and development for our SDRs. The Sales Development Manager holds ultimate responsibility for the team's pipeline success and team culture. As such, this leader should be experienced in partnering effectively with cross-functional leaders across the GTM organization, from Sales and Marketing to Operations and Enablement.   We need someone who is confident and decisive but also humble, empathetic  and open-minded. While there is a massive opportunity for Grafana Labs in the NORAM region, there are also problems to solve and building to be done. We need someone who enjoys a fast-paced environment but who prioritizes intentionality and quality, and who sees these challenges as opportunities.   What You’ll Be Doing: This is a 1st line management role, where you’ll develop and mentor a team of SDRs, including responsibility for performance management, recruitment, and training Help execute on the strategy to ensure the success of our open source users and pipeline generation. Work cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, Operations, Enablement, and Recruiting Take an analytical and data-driven approach to your business with strong instincts, decisiveness to influence change and drive improved productivity. Drive an inclusive, collaborative environment, where there is constant learning and growth.  What Makes You a Great Fit: 3 years of first-line management and/or experience in sales, sales development, operations, or enablement. Consistent track record of leading teams to exceed targets within a fast-paced and technical client acquisition driven business.  Ability to operate in an entrepreneurial, remote environment Growth mindset, leading by example & proactively bringing solutions to challenges you identify, backed by data. Experience with Salesforce, prospecting tools, MEDDPICC, value based selling (Force Management). The Grafana SDR function is building an AI-native workflow layer: account research, persona research, list building, and personalized outbound, systematized from the output of our best SDRs. Be a practitioner voice in that build, shaping the workflows, and holding the standard across EMEA and APAC alongside regional peers. Located in the United States. Compensation & Rewards: In the United States, the OTE (On-Target Earnings) compensation range for this role is $ 138,000  - $159,200. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes and RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. Other benefits included in the US are listed here. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 100% Remote, Global Culture -  As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things. Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work. Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics. Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career. Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human. Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do. In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.  Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp is hiring a Customer Activation Manager for Ramp Accounts Receivable , which brings the work behind getting paid into one connected workflow. You will help finance teams make invoicing, follow-up on unpaid balances, payment matching, and accounting handoffs useful and repeatable. You will own the customer-facing implementation and adoption plan, partner with the broader account team and specialists as needed, and help build a clear playbook for future launches. This role is a strong fit for a customer success or implementation professional who understands finance workflows and enjoys creating structure as a product grows. What You’ll Do Discover how customers create invoices, follow up on unpaid balances, match payments, handle exceptions, and update their accounting records. Choose a practical first workflow with the customer, then lead the plan from setup through first use, training, and repeat adoption. Align Controllers, AR operators, account teams, and technical partners on prerequisites, responsibilities, decisions, and timelines. Identify and resolve adoption blockers, and escalate payment-matching or accounting integration issues with clear evidence and context. Communicate customer progress and value in terms of time saved, visibility, and a more reliable invoice-to-cash process. Document customer learnings in reusable discovery, onboarding, and handoff practices. What You’ll Need Roughly 3+ years of relevant experience in customer success, onboarding, implementations, or a related customer-facing role; level is flexible based on experience. A record of personally leading post-sale implementation or workflow adoption from discovery through first use and continued use. Ability to map a finance workflow, find manual handoffs or blockers, and turn the findings into a practical customer plan. Clear communication with finance stakeholders and cross-functional partners, including ownership of next steps and thoughtful escalation. Comfort working without a mature playbook and improving the process for future customers. Nice to Haves Direct experience with accounts receivable, invoicing, billing, collections, cash application, or payment matching. Familiarity with accounting software, ERP integrations, or accounting-system handoffs. Experience in finance software or with finance-led customer implementations. descriptionAr: About Us At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale. With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world. Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater. About the Role You will be LangChain's dedicated cloud alliance lead for AWS, owning the relationships and revenue motions that make these partnerships produce real pipeline. This is a senior individual contributor role sitting within the Partnerships team where you'll be close to the product, close to the field, and expected to drive results without a lot of hand-holding. You'll own co-sell execution and marketplace presence end-to-end, working with cloud partner teams, field sellers, and LangChain's GTM organization to turn partner relationships into closed deals. What You'll Do Co-sell and pipeline Own and grow LangChain's co-sell motion with AWS: manage joint pipeline, coordinate deals with AWS field teams, and drive sourced and influenced revenue. Partner with LangChain sales leadership to define priority co-sell accounts, map territories to AWS coverage, and run co-sell plays region by region. Keep ACE hygiene high across the sales team so that opportunity sharing, acceptance, and launch become routine rather than a partnerships-team chore. Marketplace Own LangChain's AWS Marketplace presence end to end: listings, private offers, CPPO through channel partners, and program enrollment. Operate our marketplace GTM platform (Suger today) and extend referral and offer automation so sellers can transact through Marketplace without partnerships-team involvement. Programs and funding Operationalize AWS funding mechanisms across the team: MDF (market development funds for co-marketing), proof-of-concept credits, ISV Accelerate benefits, and any strategic collaboration funding we secure. Pursue AWS competency and specialization programs that strengthen our positioning with AWS sellers. Track funding drawn down against funding available and report it monthly. Executive and partner relationships Own LangChain's working relationships at AWS: partner development managers, ISV sales managers, Marketplace category leads, and the Bedrock and AgentCore partner teams. Build executive sponsorship on both sides, and run a joint business plan with AWS that sets shared goals and a review cadence. Navigate the coopetitive dynamic: partner closely with AWS on Bedrock and AgentCore while differentiating LangGraph and LangSmith where AWS has competing offerings. Field enablement and marketing Equip LangChain sales, solutions engineering, and marketing with better-together messaging, competitive positioning, and joint sales plays for AWS accounts. Partner with marketing on co-branded campaigns, content, and events that generate pipeline, including re:Invent, AWS Summits, and joint customer programs. Communicate results clearly to internal stakeholders, including a monthly readout on pipeline, Marketplace, and program activity. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.   The Opportunity: Grafana Labs is looking for a technically fluent engineer who loves building powerful demos, explaining complex systems clearly, and helping SRE and platform engineering leaders understand the value of our open approach to observability. As Grafana’s offering shifts from dashboards to industry-leading agentic observability, our Product Marketing team is responsible for closing the gap between what our products can do and how customers understand that value. That means building clear, consistent positioning, enabling sellers with trustworthy technical narratives, and creating content that helps Platform Engineering teams quickly grasp why Grafana Cloud is the right choice for them. As a Technical Product Marketer you will play a critical part in that transformation. You’ll be the hands-on engineer who brings our technical story to life for buyers, not just practitioners. You’ll build core demos, run technical workshops and webinars, and act as the technical bridge between our Product and Sales orgs. Your work will help SRE and platform engineering leaders evaluate Grafana with confidence, equip sales engineers with better tools and talk tracks, and ensure our technical value shows up clearly and consistently across the entire customer journey. This is a unique chance to shape how Grafana tells its story as we evolve our positioning in the AI era, strengthen seller enablement, and build a repeatable system for communicating product value. What You'll Be Doing: Build strategic, buyer-focused demos, videos, workshops, and webinars Create and maintain polished, narrative-driven demos that highlight Grafana’s value for SRE and platform engineering leaders. Record high-quality technical demo videos and walkthroughs in partnership with our video and content teams. Lead webinars, workshops, and technical sessions designed for evaluators. Teach customers not just how Grafana works, but why our approach is differentiated and valuable. Use AI tools to generate variations, summaries, and reusable assets that scale technical content across channels. Enable Solutions (Sales) Engineers with clear, consistent technical storytelling Serve as PMM’s technical liaison to the SE org, ensuring consistent messaging and demo guidance. Produce technical enablement assets, value-driven talk tracks, competitive narratives, and demo best practices. Help SEs and sellers communicate Grafana’s story with clarity, confidence, and differentiation. Collaborate with PMMs to drive technical buyer engagement across high-impact channels Partner with PMMs to identify the most important buyer personas, problems, and technical messages, and help shape the content strategy needed to reach them. Extend technical narratives into impactful buyer-facing channels including analyst briefings (Gartner, Forrester), industry forums, podcasts, conferences, and online technical communities. Bring a technical perspective to PMM planning—helping ensure our content, campaigns, and enablement reflect the real challenges and priorities of SREs and engineering leaders. Use automation & AI to scale technical content Partner with software engineers to streamline demo setup, content workflows, and asset updates through workflows, agents, scripts, and AI-driven tools. Use automation to make technical content more repeatable, discoverable, and scalable across teams. What Makes You a Great Fit: 5+ years in a technical role (solutions engineering, SRE, DevOps, backend engineering, technical PMM, or similar). Interest and ability to travel to training and customer events 10-12 weeks per year. Strong understanding of observability concepts and the needs of SRE/platform teams. Ability to translate deep technical concepts into clear, value-focused stories. Experience presenting technical content through demos, workshops, or webinars. Excellent written and verbal communication, with a crisp, structured, persuasive style. Strong cross-functional collaboration; comfort working with PMM, Product, SEs, DevRel, and Field Engineering. High ownership mindset with the ability to drive projects from concept to completion. Comfort with light scripting or workflow automation. Bonus Points For: Hands-on experience with Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Mimir, Tempo, or similar observability tools, or a background in Observability or Platform Engineering. Prior experience in Sales Engineering, DevRel, or technical product marketing. Familiarity with demo environment automation or infrastructure-as-code tools. Exceptional live presentation or workshop facilitation skills. Compensation & Rewards: In Germany, the ba

Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission. Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network. The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base. The Role CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core. Rapid response. When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare's infrastructure and the customer's stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation. Proactive engineering. When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds. Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline. Partner with a government customer's SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring. You will work from concept through factory testing, site commissioning, performance validation, and operational improvement. Evaluate cybersecurity, redundancy, time synchronization, communications protocols, data quality, and remote-support requirements. Lead or support software reviews, simulator testing, factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning, and tuning. Troubleshoot control-system and plant-performance issues and convert findings into corrective actions and reusable standards. Partner with electrical, mechanical, CSA, IT, security, operations, OEM, EPC, and data center controls teams. Qualifications 8+ years of controls, automation, or instrumentation engineering experience in power generation, industrial plants, utilities, or mission-critical infrastructure. Strong experience with PLC, DCS, SCADA, historian, industrial-networking, and control-system integration. Knowledge of generation controls, synchronization, load sharing, protective interfaces, process control, and safety interlocks. Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures. Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries. Understanding of industrial cybersecurity, redundancy, failover, and change-control practices. Bachelor's degree in controls, electrical, mechanical, chemical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field. Experience with IEC 61850, Modbus, OPC UA, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, or comparable industrial protocols. Experience integrating generation controls with BMS, EPMS, DCIM, or utility systems. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network. We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service. About the Role As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer, you will oversee the quality of data center equipment at supplier factories. You will use production data, audits, and test results to identify systemic, recurring, or safety-related issues and work with suppliers to address them through Closed Loop Learning (CLL). You will work with suppliers and internal teams to define inspections and factory tests for each type of equipment. You will coordinate issue resolution before shipment and manage deviations across multiple suppliers and project sites. Key Responsibilities Manufacturing Monitoring and Supplier Improvement Manufacturing monitoring: Work with Manufacturing Operations to monitor production progress, quality controls, inspection results, and test readiness. Flag emerging risks and coordinate a response with suppliers. Product and process audits: Audit products and processes during and after production against engineering requirements, critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure. Manufacturing coordination: Agree on production checkpoints and inspection and testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery. Manufacturing scorecards: Develop supplier and product scorecards with Manufacturing Operations. Review audit findings, test results, recurring defects, and open issues with suppliers to prioritize improvements. Drive continuous improvement: Lead the CLL process with suppliers. Track root cause analyses and corrective and preventive actions in a shared register. Verify that each action addresses the underlying problem before closing it. Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) Standardize requirements and formats: Develop product-specific FAT requirements and standard test formats with equipment suppliers and OpenAI’s engineering, commissioning, quality, and Manufacturing Operations teams. Define critical quality requirements: Document the CTQ characteristics each test must verify in an OpenAI-accepted format. Use CLL findings to revise FAT procedures so future tests check for known failure modes. Ensure auditable supplier records: Require suppliers to retain test results and make them available for OpenAI audits. Manage documentation and revision control: Review final FAT records and audit reports for each piece of equipment and maintain a controlled revision history. Conduct periodic supplier audits: Check that suppliers follow approved test procedures and that their records accurately reflect the tests performed. Factory Witness Testing (FWT) Align checklists and stakeholders: Develop standard FWT checklists with OpenAI subject matter experts, installing contractors, and the construction management team. Agree on requirements before testing begins. Manage documentation and reporting: Collect and review final witness test reports and supporting records from participants. Before shipment, confirm that each witness-test issue is resolved or covered by a documented deviation. Log systemic, recurring, or safety-related findings in the CLL tracker and verify the effectiveness of corrective actions with the supplier. Ability to develop test checklists, define CTQs, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records. Experience monitoring supplier production, auditing products and processes during and after production, and using scorecards to improve supplier and product quality. Experience managing controlled documents and deviations. Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple pieces of equipment. Ability to communicate quality requirements and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, quality, and construction teams. Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40–60% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites. Preferred Skills Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems. Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments. A global platform which is within approximately 50 milliseconds of about 95% of the Internet connected population, serving on average, over 46 million HTTP requests per second. The Performance Team owns overall system and application performance across that fleet: resource optimization, instrumentation, and the tooling that lets us see what the hardware is actually doing. System memory sits alongside CPU cycles, network processing, and storage IOPS as a first-class resource, and how the kernel manages it is increasingly the thing that decides how hot we can safely run every machine we own. We work upstream first. Several of us maintain or regularly contribute to the Linux kernel, and our default is to fix problems in mainline rather than carry private patches. This role is built on that principle. The problem you would own Using memory efficiently is one of the highest-leverage problems we have. At our scale, how the kernel's memory-management subsystem behaves under pressure has direct consequences for both performance and cost. As DRAM prices climb, getting more out of the memory we already own is a real lever on infrastructure spend. Using custom low-overhead instrumentation on production servers, we have identified several scalability bottlenecks in the kernel memory layer that show up under real workloads. We are looking for an expert to take on these problems, fix them against production workloads, and drive the changes upstream. Solving them lifts efficiency and latency across the entire fleet rather than in one place. What you will do Diagnose and fix performance and scalability bottlenecks in the Linux kernel memory-management subsystem, informed by real production telemetry at a scale few environments can offer. Land your work upstream. We expect MM changes to go to mainline first and want you to keep doing the maintainership and review work that earns standing in the community. Build and extend low-overhead kernel instrumentation (tracepoints, BPF, perf) so we keep measuring before we change, and prove the impact afterwards. Partner with kernel, networking, storage, and product engineers across the company to turn observed system behavior into concrete MM improvements. Set technical direction for how Cloudflare uses, tunes, and evolves kernel memory management as we push utilization higher. You will work directly with Sales leadership, Revenue Operations, Enablement, and the data and engineering teams on tools that save sellers real time. Success is identified by creating systems that resolve mundane tasks and save people real time. Comfort working directly in BigQuery, Snowflake, or a similar warehouse. Experience integrating SaaS systems over REST APIs and webhooks, and tracing a failure back to its source. Working knowledge of enrichment and signal tools such as D&B, ZoomInfo, and HG Insights, and a view on what to do when two sources disagree. You can explain the same system to a sales VP in two sentences and to an engineer in a schema, and you can influence leaders on teams that don't report to you. Available Locations: Austin or London About the Role TLS is the connective tissue of the Internet, and Cloudflare terminates a large fraction of it. Every day, our network handles certificate operations across products like Universal SSL, SSL for SaaS, Origin CA, Cloudflare Access, and Cloudflare Tunnel. We intend to be ACME-first, automation-first, and transparent by design. You will work across product, engineering, security, compliance, legal, operations, sales, marketing, and the WebPKI ecosystem to turn Cloudflare's CA from a major technical commitment into a product customers trust and adopt. This is an early-days role on a growing team. It is not a role for someone who only manages backlog. The right person will be comfortable with high-consequence infrastructure, deep customer discovery, ecosystem trust, compliance scrutiny, and zero-to-one product building. The decisions you make in the first year will shape how Cloudflare participates in the certificate authority market for years to come. Responsibilities Define the product strategy for Cloudflare's CA business  across publicly trusted certificates, certificate lifecycle automation, ACME issuance, renewal workflows, revocation, Certificate Transparency, customer controls, developer experience, and integrations with Cloudflare's broader platform. Make resilience a product principle.  Help design product requirements that fail small, reduce customer blast radius, support automated recovery, and make certificate replacement fast enough to handle compliance issues, revocation events, or ecosystem incidents. Drive an ACME-first customer experience  that makes it easy for users of existing free or automated CAs to adopt Cloudflare with minimal tooling changes. Partner with compliance, legal, security, and operations  to ensure product decisions align with CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, WebTrust audits, root store program policies, Certificate Policy and Certification Practice Statement commitments, and public incident response expectations. descriptionAr: About MotherDuck Don’t let the quirky name fool you: At MotherDuck , we’re on a mission to make data warehousing fun, frictionless, and ducking awesome for developers and data practitioners building blazing fast internal and customer-facing analytics experiences. We're building a cloud-hosted version of DuckDB, working hand-in-hand with the creators of the fastest-growing and fastest-improving query engine on the planet. Unlike other databases, MotherDuck was architected to unify local development with cloud operations to bridge the gap between software and data engineering workflows. Our team is a mix of thoughtful, passionate, and empathetic data industry veterans. What you will do We’re looking for a Product Marketer who lives at the intersection of words, product, and customers. You’ll take what our engineers build and turn it into stories that make developers and data teams lean in. You’ll own positioning and messaging, write the pages people actually read, and make sure our sales team walks into every conversation ready. This role can be based in our Seattle, San Francisco or New York City office. Key responsibilities Write. A lot. Website copy, landing pages, launch posts, product one-pagers, emails. You care about every word and you know when to cut. Help shape how we tell our story. Work alongside product, sales, and leadership on who we’re for, why we’re different, and how to say it in a way a data engineer won’t roll their eyes at... then keep it fresh as the product and market evolve. Build the web and the artifacts. Ship landing pages, comparison pages, demos and interactive assets... ideally hands-on with AI tools rather than waiting in a queue for design and eng. Arm the sales team. Create battlecards, pitch decks, objection handling, and competitive takes that AEs and Customer Engineers actually use in deals. Sit in on calls and bring what you hear back into the messaging. Run launches. Plan and ship product launches end to end with product, engineering, DevRel and growth. Stay close to customers and the market. Talk to users, track competitors (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and friends), and turn what you learn into sharper stories. Work AI-first. Use Claude and other tools to research, draft, prototype and ship. Help set the bar for how marketing at MotherDuck uses AI. What you bring 3 to 10 years in product marketing, ideally at a B2B software or developer-focused company Excellent writing. Clear, punchy, and specific... you can make a technical idea land in one sentence A real knack for positioning: you've taken a product to market and can show the before and after Experience building web pages and landing pages, and comfort shipping them yourself with modern tools A track record of sales enablement that sales teams actually used Genuine curiosity about technical products. You don't need to write SQL for a living, but you want to understand how the thing works AI fluency. You already use AI daily to do better work, and you're excited to push that further A bias for action. You'd rather ship a good version this week than a perfect one next quarter What people should be saying if you’re doing ducking awesome “I sent the new landing page to a prospect and they replied ‘this is exactly our problem.’ Didn’t have to explain a thing.” “Honestly, I understand our own feature better after reading the launch post.” “The battlecard came up in the call and I had the answer before they finished the question.” “They showed me a workflow they built with AI last week and now half of marketing uses it.” What we provide Feather-ruffling compensation – competitive salary and stock options so you have a stake in our flock’s success. Top-notch healthcare coverage – 100% paid medical, dental, and vision for employees, plus 80% coverage for dependents (because we care about your whole nest). Flexible PTO – take the time you need to recharge, explore, or just have a lazy day by the pond. 401k plan – because even ducks need to plan for the future. Flexible work environment - spend most of the week in the office collaborating with the flock, and work from wherever you're most productive the rest of the time. Specifics are role dependent and as agreed upon with your manager Why MotherDuck We're a ~110-person, Series B team building on one of the fastest-growing open source projects in data. We're small enough that your work shows up on the website next week, and growing fast enough that there's always something new to figure out. How we work comes down to four values: Thoughtfulness. We care about the people we work with and the craft behind what we ship. Flexibility. Plans change. We adapt without drama. Unorthodoxy. We question the default way of doing things, including in marketing. Agency. We own outcomes and don't wait for permission. Please Apply Does this role sound appealing to you, but you’re missing some of the requirements or don’t quite think you’re qualified? Please apply anyway. Research has shown that underrepresented groups in technology often shy away from roles which aren’t a 100% match. We aim to build a diverse team and will strongly consider applicants who bring many of the requirements plus have other experiences which round out their qualifications. MotherDuck is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. MotherDuck is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with physical and mental disabilities.

Our team is a mix of thoughtful, passionate, and empathetic data industry veterans. What you will do The Database team is the bridge between DuckDB and the cloud. We own the core server and client extension logic that lets DuckDB run seamlessly, whether it's local or in the cloud, and we work in C++ right alongside the DuckDB codebase itself. Our mission is to push the boundaries of embedded database performance, distributed execution, and user experience, all while staying closely connected to DuckDB Labs (the team behind DuckDB) to align on APIs and shape what's next. Day to day, we drive major projects in dual execution, resource assignment, and system reliability, while also handling incoming issues and lending our DuckDB expertise to other teams. We collaborate closely across MotherDuck and with the wider DuckDB community, making sure people get the best of both local and cloud worlds. It's a small, high-agency team with big ambitions... the kind of place where engineers own impactful projects, share what they learn, and help shape how modern analytics gets built. This role is ideally based in Amsterdam or Berlin, but we are also open to great candidates remotely in Europe. Key Responsibilities: Own major projects in our dual execution stack, so DuckDB can process queries seamlessly whether they're running locally or in the cloud. Help build a cloud platform that dynamically assigns resources, so DuckDB stays efficient whether someone's running a tiny workload or pushing our biggest, highest-memory instances. Lead cross-functional work with our frontend, platform, and infrastructure teams to keep the user experience coherent end to end. Push the state of the art in embedded database performance, distributed execution, and DuckDB internals. Deepen your DuckDB expertise and share it with the rest of the company through mentorship and documentation. Work directly with our support team to debug issues, learn from real usage patterns, and prioritize the improvements that matter most. Improve systems holistically... spotting architectural challenges early and clearing bottlenecks before they become problems. Mentor teammates and help raise the bar for engineering practices across the team. Work closely with DuckDB Labs (which grew out of the Database Architectures group at CWI, where vectorized execution and DuckDB were born) to help align on APIs and shape where DuckDB goes next. What you bring You've built and shipped complex backend systems, and you know what great looks like. You're fluent in a backend language like C++, Rust, Java, or similar systems languages, and you're comfortable working close to the metal. (C++ and Rust are the biggest plus here, and we love a great Java engineer too.) A good foundation in query engines, execution plans, indexing, and performance optimization techniques. descriptionAr: About MotherDuck Don’t let the quirky name fool you: At MotherDuck , we’re on a mission to make data warehousing fun, frictionless, and ducking awesome for developers and data practitioners building blazing fast internal and customer-facing analytics experiences. We're building a cloud-hosted version of DuckDB, working hand-in-hand with the creators of the fastest-growing and fastest-improving query engine on the planet. Unlike other databases, MotherDuck was architected to unify local development with cloud operations to bridge the gap between software and data engineering workflows. Our team is a mix of thoughtful, passionate, and empathetic data industry veterans. What you will do The Database team is the bridge between DuckDB and the cloud. We own the core server and client extension logic that lets DuckDB run seamlessly, whether it's local or in the cloud, and we work in C++ right alongside the DuckDB codebase itself. Our mission is to push the boundaries of embedded database performance, distributed execution, and user experience, all while staying closely connected to DuckDB Labs (the team behind DuckDB) to align on APIs and shape what's next. Day to day, we drive major projects in dual execution, resource assignment, and system reliability, while also handling incoming issues and lending our DuckDB expertise to other teams. We collaborate closely across MotherDuck and with the wider DuckDB community, making sure people get the best of both local and cloud worlds. It's a small, high-agency team with big ambitions... the kind of place where engineers own impactful projects, share what they learn, and help shape how modern analytics gets built. This role is ideally based in New York City but also open to great candidates remotely on the East Coast. Key Responsibilities: Own major projects in our dual execution stack, so DuckDB can process queries seamlessly whether they're running locally or in the cloud. Help build a cloud platform that dynamically assigns resources, so DuckDB stays efficient whether someone's running a tiny workload or pushing our biggest, highest-memory instances. Lead cross-functional work with our frontend, platform, and infrastructure teams to keep the user experience coherent end to end. Push the state of the art in embedded database performance, distributed execution, and DuckDB internals. Deepen your DuckDB expertise and share it with the rest of the company through mentorship and documentation. Work directly with our support team to debug issues, learn from real usage patterns, and prioritize the improvements that matter most. Improve systems holistically... spotting architectural challenges early and clearing bottlenecks before they become problems. Mentor teammates and help raise the bar for engineering practices across the team. Work closely with DuckDB Labs (which grew out of the Database Architectures group at CWI, where vectorized execution and DuckDB were born) to help align on APIs and shape where DuckDB goes next. What you bring You've built and shipped complex backend systems, and you know what great looks like. You're fluent in a backend language like C++, Rust, Java, or similar systems languages, and you're comfortable working close to the metal. (C++ and Rust are the biggest plus here, and we love a great Java engineer too.) A good foundation in query engines, execution plans, indexing, and performance optimization techniques. Hands-on experience with DuckDB is a huge plus, no matter what level you're coming in at. You've worked with cloud infrastructure, networking, and building low-latency distributed systems. You can scope and lead projects that span multiple collaborators and cross-functional dependencies. You take pride in clear thinking, careful design, and thoughtful tradeoffs. You're comfortable mentoring peers and helping build a collaborative, high-agency environment. You enjoy engaging with the wider community, whether that's open-source conversations or working directly with DuckDB Labs. Flexible PTO – take the time you need to recharge, explore, or just have a lazy day by the pond. 401k plan – because even ducks need to plan for the future. Legendary company events – we bring the flock together twice a year for unforgettable team gatherings a year to keep our bonds strong. descriptionAr: About the Team The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows. The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn country priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements. We combine product strategy, product experimentation, with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets. Build and execute a focused international growth roadmap, including in-product upsell, cross-sell, targeting, onboarding, activation/adoption, expansion, and monetization related experiences. Identify the use cases, onboarding barriers, product entry points, and upgrade moments that can improve adoption and sustained customer value. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s Legal team plays a crucial role in advancing our mission by tackling innovative and fundamental legal issues in AI. The team includes professionals from diverse legal fields—technology, AI, infrastructure, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation—who collaborate closely with colleagues across the company. If you are passionate about being an energy and infrastructure lawyer working on cutting-edge challenges, you’ll thrive here. About the Role We’re seeking an experienced energy lawyer to support the business on legal matters relating to the energy and power infrastructure supporting OpenAI’s fast-growing data center portfolio. This is a cross-functional role that will partner closely with energy, infrastructure development, engineering, procurement, and finance teams to advise on complex legal and regulatory issues and help structure, negotiate, and manage the transactions that secure reliable, cost-effective power for OpenAI’s long-term infrastructure ambitions. We’re looking for an experienced energy and infrastructure lawyer who thrives in ambiguity and wants to help define the commercial playbook for power procurement and energy project development in the AI era. This role reports to the Associate General Counsel for Infrastructure. The role’s scope and level will reflect the successful candidate’s experience and expertise. In this role, you will: Own legal strategy and risk management for OpenAI’s global energy procurement and power infrastructure transactions, from initial structuring through execution and ongoing implementation. Draft, negotiate, and advise on complex power purchase agreements, energy supply and hedging arrangements, and utility service and special contracts, including related regulatory requirements and approvals. Structure and negotiate interconnection, transmission, and utility infrastructure arrangements that align power availability with data center development and operating schedules. Advise leadership and business leaders on legal and regulatory considerations as they develop and implement our energy and data center strategy Support strategic partnerships involving renewable and other carbon-free generation, energy storage, and on-site or behind-the-meter power solutions for AI infrastructure. Develop legal and regulatory frameworks for energy procurement, project development, and collaboration with utilities, independent power producers, and energy developers. Partner with finance and operations teams to align contract terms with business and compliance requirements, including pricing, delivery and curtailment risk, credit support, and project milestones. Collaborate with policy and regulatory colleagues on issues impacting energy transactions, utility tariffs, grid access, market participation, retail service requirements, and renewable energy attributes. Build scalable, efficient contracting processes that support OpenAI’s energy and infrastructure development at speed while managing legal and regulatory risk. Guide outside counsel and coordinate with real estate, construction, tax, and regulatory counsel on energy transactions and project development. You might thrive in this role if you: 10+ years of legal experience, with substantial focus on complex commercial energy transactions. Have a JD and license or qualification to practice in CA. Relevant experience in-house, at a law firm, or a combination of both, advising energy companies, utilities, developers, major power customers, or infrastructure investors. Demonstrated experience independently leading complex energy transactions, including power purchase, utility service, or interconnection agreements. Familiarity with U.S. electricity markets, utility tariffs, and the regulatory frameworks affecting energy supply, interconnection, and transmission, including FERC, state utility commissions, and regional grid operators. Strong commercial judgment and financial fluency in energy pricing, volume commitments, credit support, and allocation of development and operating risk. Demonstrated ability to operate with autonomy and sound judgment in highly technical and fast-moving environments. Exceptional communication skills, with an ability to distill complexity into actionable, business-aligned guidance and advise senior business leaders on strategic decisions. Experience advising on cross-border energy deals and international energy regulatory frameworks is a plus. Prior experience with data center power procurement, generation or storage development, energy project finance, joint ventures, or on-site and behind-the-meter energy projects is a strong plus. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. descriptionAr: Hello! I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. 👋 Knowledge is one of the most important levers we have for delivering a great customer experience. Our knowledge ecosystem shapes how customers learn Ashby, how our Specialists resolve tickets, and how many customers never need to file a ticket at all. We have a tenured, talented Knowledge Management team doing excellent work. What we’re missing is someone to unify its work into a single, strategic practice. That’s why we’re hiring our first Director of Knowledge Management. You’ll lead a team of Knowledge Managers and expand the team into new areas, including Digital Support experience and content localization. You’ll set the vision, standards, and operating model that connect our customer-facing Help Center, internal Knowledge Base, and the self-service and in-app experiences built on them, including our AI Assistant. You’ll coach and develop a team that is growing and taking on new kinds of work, and you’ll be the voice of Knowledge in conversations with Support, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, and beyond. About the role Today, our Knowledge Managers divide their work between internal and external content. You’ll help the team decide where to focus next, in what order, and how its structure should evolve to deliver on those priorities. Knowledge Management is its own function at Ashby, separate from the internal and external enablement teams. You’ll build strong partnerships with both, defining clear boundaries and handoffs so content is consistent, never duplicated, and never left without an owner. Your team will also co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, helping customers find the right knowledge when and where they need it. You’ll stay close enough to the content to coach with specifics, while relying on your team for the day-to-day execution of knowledge governance. What you’ll own: Set the Direction for Knowledge Define the vision, roadmap, and success measures for Knowledge Management across internal and external content. Identify the highest-impact opportunities to improve the knowledge ecosystem and sequence them against team capacity. Build a clear model for content ownership, governance, and quality, streamlining how content is created, reviewed, and kept current as our product evolves. Champion Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) practices and drive adoption across Support. Lead and Develop the Team Coach and develop Knowledge Managers through specific feedback on their work, clear career paths, and growth opportunities. Evolve the team’s structure and divide work in the way that best serves customers and the business, with room to move beyond the current internal/external split. Hire and onboard new team members next year, including Knowledge Managers, a Digital Support experience role, and a localization role. Shape the AI Assistant’s Self-Service Experience Co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, aligning on strategy, roadmap, and quality and partnering with Support, Support Operations, and Engineering on design and testing. Help lead both declarative flows (structured, designed paths) and generative flows (AI-composed answers grounded in our content), and decide when each is the right tool. Shape how content is structured, tagged, and governed so the Assistant surfaces accurate, current answers. Build Our Localization Strategy Build our localization strategy for Help Center content and drive the translation strategy for Customer Education, balancing quality, speed, and cost. Define priorities for languages, content types, and tooling, and put processes in place to keep translated content in sync with the source. Measure and Improve Results Define and report on knowledge health, including content usage, search success, deflection, article quality, freshness, and the impact of knowledge on ticket volume and handle time. Treat deflection as a signal of customer success, not just cost reduction. Measure how well the AI Assistant resolves customer questions, and use those conversations, ticket trends, customer feedback, and Specialist input to identify gaps and set content priorities. Partner Across Ashby Work closely with Customer Education and internal enablement in RevOps to align on ownership, standards, and a shared view of the customer and employee learning journey. Partner with Product Marketing and Engineering so documentation keeps pace with releases and launches. Requirements Multiple years of experience leading knowledge management or content programs, setting strategy and building processes that scale with the business, ideally in B2B SaaS Support or Customer Experience. Experience managing a team of content or knowledge professionals, including coaching people at different levels of experience. Ability to connect knowledge across internal and external audiences, aligning Support, Product, Marketing, Engineering, and enablement teams around clear ownership and shared standards. Experience designing or operating self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including both structured and generative flows, and a point of view on how knowledge quality shapes their performance. Experience defining success measures for knowledge and using data to prioritize and make tradeoffs. Comfort working in ambiguity as the function’s first dedicated leader, building on existing practices while setting a clear direction. Strong writing and editing instincts. You’ll stay close enough to the work to set a high quality bar and give specific feedback. Experience with KCS or comparable methodologies. You should apply if: You’ve led a knowledge management, documentation, or content program and managed a team of knowledge or content professionals. You’ve designed or operated self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including structured and generative flows, and understand how knowledge quality affects their performance. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity: Make a difference. Are you looking for something new in your career? Our Enterprise Solutions Engineering team are our in-house, customer-facing product experts.  The Enterprise SE team enables Grafana Labs worldwide growth by educating potential and existing customers to ensure they are happy and successful.  We share our technical and product expertise with customers through demos, hands-on enablement, presentations, technical evaluations and ongoing interaction.
