What You’ll Be Doing: Join as an early member of a high growth team working together to solve technical and customer problems the right way Partner with our Sales team to articulate the overall Grafana value proposition, vision, and strategy to customers Own the technical engagement with customers and help to close high-velocity opportunities through advanced competitive knowledge, technical skill, and credibility Deliver product and technical presentations to potential and existing customers Proactively communicate with customers and internal teams to provide a feedback loop on our products and the competitive landscape Drive product conversations based on need and problems learned during customer interactions Work with the team to enhance documentation, write blog posts, record videos, contribute knowledge base articles, and create other public and internal enablement material What Makes You a Great Fit: Ideally located in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Chicago, Michigan, Indiana, Ohio 5+ years of technical pre-sales experience, ideally with Open Source technologies, or in the Metrics/Monitoring space while we will be adding more junior folks later on, right now we just need team members that can hit the ground running. We’re a startup so your job duties will be varied and complex and will require strong judgment, collaboration, and leadership We are a remote-first company so you would need to learn to work and collaborate with an international team You will need first class written and oral communication skills to collaborate with our remote-first internal teams and with our worldwide customers. You will need to be able to skillfully articulate our value proposition and the technical advantages of our products You will love solving technical challenges and thrive on bringing creative solutions to our customers You should have a technical mindset and a desire to grow technically. Great candidates may be a recent grad of a coding bootcamp or have previous post-sales or engineering experience–we are excited to see what unique experiences and skill sets you bring to the table!   You are self-motivated, initiative, creative, and maybe you’ve already done a brave thing or two in your life!   Compensation & Rewards: In the United States the OTE (On-Target Earnings) compensation range for this role is $204,000 - $254,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. Practical knowledge of cloud computing concepts and related technologies, with the ability to discuss deployment, security, and operations options with technical teams. descriptionAr: About the Team Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models. We work across research, engineering, product, and policy to understand risks, develop and validate safeguards, and support responsible deployment. Our work spans safeguards research and deployment, safety assessments, launch readiness, and trusted-access programs for advanced capabilities. We address risks including biological and cyber misuse and misalignment, with programs that strengthen safety across models and products. About the Role We’re hiring Research Program Managers across AI Safeguards and Frontier Risks Safety. You’ll lead programs that develop and improve the safeguards used across our models and products, or assess and mitigate risks associated with frontier capabilities, launches, and trusted-access programs. You will partner with researchers, engineers, and other stakeholders to turn open safety questions into clear programs of work. You’ll shape technical roadmaps, coordinate execution, and use evidence to guide priorities and inform development and deployment decisions. We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience managing complex research programs, and a commitment to AI safety. These roles are based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Shape safety programs and technical roadmaps. Partner with research and engineering leads to define goals, milestones, dependencies, and success criteria. Prioritize intake and emerging findings, resolve blockers, and balance immediate safety needs with longer-term research and platform investments. Drive safeguards development and deployment. Translate safety research into safeguards across models and products. Maintain an end-to-end view of safeguard coverage, effectiveness, and opportunities for improvement for one or more risk areas, and drive a roadmap that advances across launches. Coordinate evaluations and safety assessments. Organize capability evaluations, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including risks from autonomous and multi-agent systems. Support embedded assessments throughout model development, internal use, and deployment. Drive safety readiness and trusted-access programs. Coordinate safety requirements and execution across frontier model launches and deployments. Work with technical teams to define assessment scope and the evidence needed to inform safety and access decisions. Turn findings into improvements. Triage safeguard gaps, jailbreaks, and overflagging with accountable teams. Establish owners and escalation paths, track remediation and regression testing, and turn recurring issues into research and engineering improvements. Strengthen the evidence behind safety decisions. Support safety cases that connect claims to evaluations, safeguards, assumptions, and remaining uncertainty. Surface evidence gaps and unresolved risks, and communicate methods, results, limitations, and follow-up actions through assessment reports, system cards, and updates to decision-makers. Build programs that scale across products. Coordinate shared tooling and feedback workflows, privacy and security requirements, and safeguard user experience and quality assurance. Help teams apply safeguards consistently across product surfaces and upcoming launches. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 5+ years of experience in technical safety work, owning technical programs, or related roles in fast-moving environments. Have led complex research or technical programs involving researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences. Understand frontier AI safety concepts, including capability evaluations, alignment, control, monitoring, and safeguard robustness, and can engage substantively with technical teams. Can assess what evaluation results do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and the difference between model capability and real-world risk. Can turn ambiguous questions into clear programs, make practical tradeoffs, and adjust priorities as evidence changes. Have worked extensively across research, engineering, and product teams and can coordinate with policy and communications partners. Exercise sound judgment when findings are concerning or incomplete, raise unresolved risks constructively, and communicate complex technical work clearly. Are motivated to help ensure increasingly capable AI systems remain beneficial and under meaningful human control. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement . Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. descriptionAr: Perplexity's sales organization is growing fast, and our sellers need the right content, tools and AI workflows to win. As our first Sales Enablement Operations Manager, you'll be the strategic partner and builder behind how Perplexity's sales team finds, uses and learns from content. This role is both strategic and hands-on. You'll work with the Sales Enablement Lead to define our content management strategy, including whether to build on Perplexity's own AI platform or buy a dedicated tool. Then you'll build it, run it and keep improving it. You'll also build AI skills, plugins and workflows that make reps and managers faster and more effective every day. This is a foundational hire. We're looking for someone who can grow into a leadership role as the enablement function scales. Responsibilities Help shape content and knowledge strategy Partner with the Sales Enablement Lead to define the long-term content management strategy for the sales team, from requirements to the build-vs-buy decision. Work alongside the Sales Enablement Lead on the evaluation: gather stakeholder needs, assess options (including Perplexity Computer and third-party platforms), model costs and tradeoffs, and shape a joint recommendation to sales leadership. Design the content architecture: taxonomy, ownership, governance, approval workflows and lifecycle (create, review, update, retire). Help build and run the enablement stack Own the implementation and maintenance of the sales content hub, call library and training platform, leveraging Perplexity throughout. Help coordinate with Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, Product and Legal so content is accurate, approved and available where sellers work (Salesforce, Slack, call-recording tools). Own enablement reporting: content usage, training completion, certification status and how they relate to ramp and performance. Build AI tools for the sales team Design, build and maintain AI skills, plugins and agent workflows for account executives, BDRs and sales managers, such as account research, call prep, deal reviews, coaching and pipeline hygiene. Turn repeated seller and manager tasks into reusable AI workflows, then drive adoption through training, documentation and feedback loops. Develop training materials for sellers and managers on using AI tools well, and keep a shared library of best practices. Lead and scale Set the standards for how enablement content and AI tools get built, contributed and maintained across the GTM organization. Act as a trusted thought partner to enablement leadership on priorities, operating model and tooling. Help shape the enablement operations function as the team grows, with a path to leading it. What we're looking for 4–6 years in go-to-market roles, with at least 2 years owning sales enablement operations, revenue operations, GTM systems or sales content strategy. Experience owning a sales content or knowledge system end to end, including taxonomy, governance, adoption and measurement. A track record of leading or heavily shaping a tooling decision, such as a platform evaluation, migration or in-house build. Real, hands-on AI fluency: you've built AI tools or workflows (custom GPTs, Claude or Perplexity skills, MCP connectors, n8n, Zapier, Clay or similar) that other people use regularly, and you can show examples. Systems thinking: you understand how content, CRM, call-recording and communication tools connect, and you design for how sellers actually work. Strong judgment and the ability to make a clear recommendation and defend it with leadership. Experience driving cross-functional projects without formal authority. Clear written and verbal communication, and a bias toward shipping, measuring and iterating. Nice to have Experience as the first enablement operations or GTM systems hire, building the function from scratch. Hands-on experience with enablement platforms such as Highspot, Seismic, Guru, Mindtickle or Showpad. Background as an AE, SE or BDR before moving into enablement or operations. Experience managing or mentoring contractors, interns or direct reports. Experience at a high-growth AI or SaaS company. What success looks like First 90 days: You've assessed current content and tools, interviewed sellers and managers, made a build-vs-buy recommendation with the Sales Enablement Lead, and shipped the first AI skills the sales team uses every week. First 6 months: A governed content hub and call library are live and adopted, enablement reporting is in place, and a growing library of AI tools is measurably saving time for reps and managers. First year: Enablement operations is a scalable function with clear standards, and you're ready to lead it as the team grows.

We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? Cohere is in a unique and exciting position to grow our go-to-market teams globally! We are expanding our Talent Team and are looking for creative, high-performing talent sourcers who are eager to take on a new challenge as we are in the early stages of building the Talent Acquisition function. In this role, you will master a new domain of sourcing, source world-class business talent, and influence the scaling of a high-growth Canadian tech company. If you consider yourself resilient, collaborative, influential, and a lifelong learner with an established network, we’d love to hear from you! In this intermediate level role you will: Build, own, and nurture a strong pipeline of world-class business talent across Sales, Finance, Revenue, Marketing & Communications, and Operations Deliver a world-class recruiting experience that reflects Cohere's premium brand Partner with hiring managers and talent partners to find and engage passive talent through creative sourcing methods Maintain deep market intelligence on business talent trends and competitive landscape Manage comprehensive recruiting funnels in our ATS, updating progress and analytics regularly Develop creative, proactive sourcing approaches to optimize the top of the funnel for business roles Cultivate relationships with established networks across business communities and industry leaders Identify and own additional high-impact talent projects as they emerge Who you are: You have 3 -7 years of experience sourcing for business roles across Sales, Finance, Revenue, Marketing & Communications, and Operations in markets like EMEA/US etc. You have a proven track record of sourcing candidates in high-growth and a high-bar environments (startup, technology, AI experience strongly preferred) You bring an established, high-profile network in business communities You're a creative problem solver who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments You're a natural influencer with exceptional relationship-building skills You leverage data and analytics to drive sourcing decisions and measure effectiveness You're passionate about diversity, equity, and building inclusive business teams You have a strategic mindset with the ability to see beyond immediate hiring needs Why Cohere Impact: Shape the future of AI talent at a cutting-edge company. Culture: Collaborative, innovative, and mission-driven. Growth: Join a team scaling from 800 to 2000+ over 18 months. Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. How and Where We Work: Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form , and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

The ability to build trusted partnerships, advise leaders and People teams, resolve ambiguity, and move decisions forward without relying on formal authority. Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to coordinate with global partners across time zones using asynchronous practices. Helpful, but not required: experience supporting a global, distributed workforce, including partners in India or other locations outside the United States; compensation-cycle communications; and experience in a software or technology company. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity  The Solutions Engineering team are the customer facing product experts. The team enables Grafana Labs worldwide growth by educating potential and existing customers to ensure that they are happy and successful. We share our technical and product expertise with customers through demos, hands on enablement, presentations, technical evaluations and ongoing interaction. We partner closely with our Sales team to help qualify and close opportunities. The Solutions Engineering team is one of the primary routes of communication from our customers to the Product Management and Engineering teams. A Solutions Engineer is able to really listen to a prospect or customer, understand their requirements, ask the right questions to extract as much information as required and translate all that into a solution with Grafana Labs technology. They are the bridge between the highly technical engineering folks here at Grafana Labs, our customers and our Sales team. What You'll Be Doing Partnering with our Sales team to articulate the overall Grafana value proposition, vision and strategy to customers Owning the technical engagement with customers and help close complex opportunities through advanced competitive knowledge, technical skill and credibility Delivering product and technical presentations to potential and existing customers Effectively communicate with customers and internal teams to provide feedback on our products and the competitive landscape Driving product conversations based on need and problems with customers Working with the team to enhance documentation, write blog posts, record videos, contribute knowledge base articles and create other public or private enablement material What Makes you a Great Fit: 5+ years of technical pre-sales experience Be open to various and complex assignments, this will require strong judgment, collaboration, and leadership You will need first class written and oral communication skills to collaborate with our remote-first internal teams and with our worldwide customers. You will need to be able to skillfully articulate our value proposition and the technical advantages of our products You love solving technical challenges and thrive on bringing creative solutions to our customers You should have a technical mindset and a desire to grow technically.  Must be located in United Kingdom   Bonus Points For: Experience with Open Source technologies, or in the Metrics/Monitoring space is an advantage  Experience with sales methodologies like MEDD(P)ICC is a plus Compensation & Rewards  In the UK, the OTE (On-Target Earnings) compensation range for this role is £123,000 - £148,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. As an agentic software creation platform, Replit lets anyone, from individual creators to teams inside the world’s largest companies, turn natural language into applications, internal tools, dashboards, and websites that solve real problems. We are looking for a Head of Corporate Affairs - Strategy & Growth to help lead Replit’s next chapter of enterprise expansion, strategic relationship building, and institutional engagement. This is a senior, commercially minded role for a strategic, hands-on leader who can turn relationships across government and industry into real opportunities for Replit. As Replit grows from a beloved developer platform into a defining company in AI and enterprise transformation, you will build the relationships and pathways that accelerate adoption across the public and private sectors. The role sits at the intersection of corporate affairs, business development, public sector strategy, and enterprise growth. It is not a traditional government relations role focused on policy, access, or reputation. You will build a repeatable, measurable approach to turning senior-level engagement into qualified pipeline, adoption, and long-term value, working closely with the President of Public Sector and Corporate Affairs, the executive team, and sales and go-to-market leaders. Role Lead the growth strategy for Corporate Affairs, turning senior-level relationships across government and industry into revenue opportunities and pipeline. Identify target accounts across government and industry, and prioritize building C-suite relationships that accelerate enterprise adoption. Partner with business development, sales, and go-to-market leaders to align outreach, create pathways into target organizations, and convert executive engagement into qualified opportunities. Develop repeatable playbooks for executive engagement and institutional partnerships, establishing a scalable relationship-to-revenue motion. Build the operating cadence, metrics, and reporting to measure Corporate Affairs’ contribution to pipeline development, enterprise growth, and adoption. Represent Replit in senior-level meetings, industry forums, and government engagements to strengthen strategic relationships and advance business opportunities. Qualifications BA/BS degree or equivalent practical experience. 10+ years of experience in corporate affairs, strategic partnerships, business development, public sector strategy, enterprise sales, government relations, government, or related fields. Experience building or significantly expanding a relationship-driven growth, partnerships, or business development function at a fast-growing technology company or similarly complex organization. Strong understanding of enterprise and public sector go-to-market motions, including how procurement, stakeholder alignment, and internal champions influence adoption. Strong executive presence and communication skills, with credibility among C-suite leaders, government officials, and technical stakeholders. Ability to translate complex technical products and AI capabilities into clear business value. A creative, resourceful, “do more with less” mindset, with the ability to build new programs without an established playbook. Passion for Replit’s mission and for AI-powered software creation expanding who can build software. This is a full-time role that can be held from our Foster City, CA office. The role has an in-office requirement of Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Full-Time Employee Benefits Include: 💰 Competitive Salary & Equity 💹 401(k) Program with a 4% match ( US Only ) ⚕️ Health, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance 🩼 Short Term and Long Term Disability 🚼 Paid Parental, Medical, Caregiver Leave 🏝 Flexible Time Off (FTO) + Holidays 🚗 Commuter Benefits ( In-Office & US Only ) 📱 Monthly Wellness Stipend 🧑‍💻 Autonomous Work Environment 🖥 In Office Set-Up Reimbursement ( In-Office Only ) 🚀 Quarterly Team Gatherings ☕ In Office Amenities ( In-Office Only ) Want to learn more about what we are up to? Self-driving Company Replit Agent at Scale AI Adoption Build Open-Source Apps Interviewing + Culture at Replit Operating Principles Reasons not to work at Replit To achieve our mission of making programming more accessible around the world, we need our team to be representative of the world. We encourage people from all kinds of backgrounds to apply, including and especially candidates from underrepresented and non-traditional backgrounds.

We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next. About the role We’re hiring the first AI Deployment Manager to partner with some of our most strategic enterprise customers. This role will be based in Sydney. As an AI Deployment Manager, you’ll drive adoption, deliver measurable business value, and help shape how AI transforms engineering teams. You’ll act as the connective tissue between customer stakeholders and our internal teams, influencing both the Grok roadmap and each customer’s implementation strategy. This role is highly cross‑functional and customer‑facing. You understand software development workflows, care deeply about developer tools, and love helping engineering organizations succeed at scale. What you'll do Build and grow deep relationships with engineering leaders and power users at key accounts Partner with Field Engineering and Sales to deliver a seamless post‑sale experience Drive adoption of Grok by aligning usage with business objectives and engineering goals Guide customers on best practices for rollout, prompt strategy, context configuration, and internal enablement Serve as the customer’s voice internally and influence roadmap priorities Provide strategic account planning and regular business reviews with VP‑ and CTO‑level stakeholders Monitor account health, usage patterns, and product engagement to drive renewals and expansion You may be a fit if You have strong communication skills and executive presence, and are comfortable whiteboarding with developers and pivoting to value with a CTO You have a deep understanding of the software development lifecycle and engineering org structures You are fluent in technical workflows, AI tooling, and developer productivity (even if you haven’t been a full‑time engineer) You are customer‑obsessed with a knack for strategic thinking and problem‑solving You thrive in a startup environment: scrappy, proactive, and adaptable You have experience in TAM, Solutions Architecture, Customer Success, or Consulting for enterprise software About Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truthseeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code. Applying If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next. Lead discovery for knowledge-work and business-process use cases and redesign high-value workflows around AI agents, enterprise tools, data, and human judgment. Help customers operationalize agents with ownership, integrations, and guardrails. Prototype alongside customers by connecting systems, designing agents and workflows, and debugging failures until ambiguous ideas become working systems. Partner with ADMs from meeting prep through active participation, and coordinate with Sales, Product, and Engineering to unblock customers. Help teams standardize on the Grok platform and embed it deeply in core workflows, and lead recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction. Shape the Future of the Product Bring structured feedback, emerging patterns, and enterprise requirements across Grok Bot and Grok Build from strategic customers into Product and Engineering. descriptionAr: About the Team The Intelligence and Investigations (I2) team provides intelligence to decision makers across OpenAI and investigates severe misuse of our products. I2’s work saves lives: we disrupt real-world violence, protect children, and prevent catastrophic harms from AI misuse. We draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership. Our analysts and investigators make sense of complex data to understand emerging risks and investigate severe misuse. They work closely with engineers who build tools that extend what human experts can see and do. The design of the investigative workflow shapes how effectively people can use those tools and act on what they learn. About the Role We’re hiring a service designer to shape how investigative cases move through OpenAI, from the first signal through review and action. You’ll work alongside investigators to understand what each case requires and how the overall workflow shapes what investigators can accomplish. You’ll bring that perspective to the people who shape investigative operations and the engineers who build the underlying systems. Together, you’ll decide where a change would help and see how it works in real cases. In this role, you will Work alongside investigators to understand how cases move across teams and systems. Consider what that process means for people at risk, people whose activity is under review, and the people responsible for acting on a finding. Combine what you learn from individual cases with operational data to decide where a change would help most and whether it calls for a change in the workflow, the tools, or both. Lead the cross-team work of mapping investigative workflows, designing improvements with the people who use and operate them, and putting agreed changes into practice. Guide engineering decisions about how investigative systems fit together to support the overall workflow. Follow changes into use. Look for whether they help investigators act in time, make well-supported decisions, and sustain demanding work. We're seeking someone with experience including: 8+ years of relevant experience in service design or closely related roles, with demonstrated ownership of improvements to complex operational workflows from research through implementation and evaluation. A bachelor’s degree in Service Design, Interaction Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Human Factors, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong qualitative research and synthesis skills, with the ability to combine insights from investigators and analysts with operational data to identify bottlenecks, inform priorities, and improve decision-making. Experience designing across internal tools, SME workflows, and systems, including how information, evidence, and decisions move between teams. Proven experience leading ambiguous projects across product, engineering, operations, and policy teams, translating evolving risks and needs into practical solutions. Experience using AI tools to support research synthesis, explore service design options, and prototype workflows, with sound judgment about sensitive information, output validation, and decisions that require human review. Clear written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to make complex workflows understandable, explain design decisions, navigate tradeoffs, and build alignment across technical and operational teams. A hands-on approach and the persistence to follow improvements through rollout, adoption, and evaluation, measuring their effect on investigation quality, timeliness, and team effectiveness. You might thrive in this role if you Have experience designing services around the needs of the people who use and run them. Enjoy learning how specialists work. You can draw on their different perspectives to understand a service that no single team sees in full. Have worked with operational and engineering teams to put a service design into practice. You’re comfortable discussing how a technical choice in one part of a workflow affects people elsewhere. Care about what happens after a design goes into use. You’re curious whether a change that helps one team also improves how a case moves through the full investigation workflow. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. descriptionAr: About the Team Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models, ensuring our models are deployed responsibly and have a positive impact on society. Our work spans diverse research and engineering initiatives—from system-level safeguards and model training to evaluation and red-teaming—all aimed at mitigating misuse and maintaining our high bar for safety. We lead OpenAI's commitment to developing and deploying safe Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), fostering a culture of trust, responsibility, and transparency. Our goal is to continuously learn from deployments, distribute AI’s benefits widely, and ensure that powerful tools remain aligned with human values and safety considerations. About the Role The Safety Measurement Research Program Manager drives OpenAI’s strategy for safety measurement and evaluations, partnering closely with safety research, data science, and engineering to advance how we measure harm and safeguard efficacy across research and production. You will work directly with researchers, data scientists, policy owners, and product teams who contribute to or use our measurement systems, identifying the most important problems to solve and shaping the data, dashboards, tools, and workflows we build for them. This role combines measurement expertise, product judgment, and cross-functional execution: you will engage with evaluation results and data workflows, make prioritization tradeoffs, and drive work from problem definition through rollout and iteration. This position is based in San Francisco, CA, with relocation assistance available. In this role, you will: Define strategic priorities and product roadmaps to improve safety measurement and evaluation approaches and scale our measurement platform to new use cases, products, and the needs of cross-functional teams Partner closely with research, data science, engineering, policy teams, and other stakeholders to craft a vision for understanding safety outcomes and prevalence across our products, and translate that vision into concrete programs of work. Drive the integration of cutting-edge AI safety research into OpenAI’s safety measurement and evaluation platforms, working with researchers, data scientists, and engineers to navigate technical tradeoffs, coordinate dependencies, and resolve blockers. Develop and continuously refine clear, actionable success criteria that effectively capture our ambitions with safety measurement and evals. Represent quantitative progress on safety to senior leadership. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 6+ years of experience in research program management, technical program management, product management, or related roles, with expertise in AI safety, trust & safety, integrity, or related domains. Have a strong foundation in data science, statistics, economics, or a related field, and hands-on experience with measurement or evaluations. Enjoy working at the intersection of data science and AI safety research, translating evolving measurement needs into clear requirements, priorities, and roadmaps. Can independently drive complex, cross-functional programs from problem definition through rollout, building alignment and unblocking decisions in ambiguous spaces. Ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions, and exercise sound judgment about technical tradeoffs and the strengths and limitations of metrics and evaluations. Build strong partnerships across research, data science, engineering, policy, and product, and communicate complex findings clearly to technical teams and leadership. Are curious about AI safety and its societal impacts, learn new domains quickly, and adapt as research and priorities evolve. descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? We are hiring for this role on a full-time contract basis to provide paternity leave coverage through the end of June 2027. Cohere is in a unique and exciting position to grow our go-to-market teams globally! We are hiring for this role on a full-time contract basis to provide paternity leave coverage through the end of June 2027 . We are looking for creative, high-performing talent partners who are eager to take on a new challenge as we are in the early stages of building the Talent Acquisition function. In this role, you will master a new domain of recruiting, hire world-class business talent, and influence the scaling of a high-growth Canadian tech company. If you consider yourself resilient, collaborative, influential, and a lifelong learner with an established network, we’d love to hear from you! As a Talent Partner, you will: Build, own, and nurture a strong pipeline of world-class business talent across People, Finance, Revenue, Marketing & Communications, and Operations Deliver a world-class recruiting experience that reflects Cohere's premium brand Partner with hiring managers and talent partners to find and engage passive talent through creative sourcing methods Maintain deep market intelligence on business talent trends and competitive landscape Manage comprehensive recruiting funnels in our ATS, updating progress and analytics regularly Develop creative, proactive sourcing approaches to optimize the top of the funnel for business roles Cultivate relationships with established networks across business communities and industry leaders Identify and own additional high-impact talent projects as they emerge Who you are: You have 5+ years of experience recruiting for business roles across Sales, Finance, Revenue, Marketing & Communications, and Operations in markets like EMEA/US etc. You have a proven track record of hiring candidates in high-growth and a high-bar environments (startup, technology, AI experience strongly preferred) You bring an established, high-profile network in business communities You're a creative problem solver who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments You're a natural influencer with exceptional relationship-building skills You leverage data and analytics to drive sourcing decisions and measure effectiveness You're passionate about diversity, equity, and building inclusive business teams You have a strategic mindset with the ability to see beyond immediate hiring needs Why Cohere Impact: Shape the future of AI talent at a cutting-edge company. Culture: Collaborative, innovative, and mission-driven. Growth: Join a team scaling from 800 to 2000+ over 18 months. Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. How and Where We Work: Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form , and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

An overview of this role As Manager, Sales Recruiting (Americas), you'll lead recruiting for Sales across the Americas, partnering with regional Sales leaders to hire the quota-carrying and go-to-market talent that supports GitLab's revenue growth. You'll develop a team of recruiters, build hiring strategies for different Sales functions and segments, and create repeatable processes that balance speed, quality, and candidate experience. You'll also stay close to the work by recruiting for senior and specialized Sales roles when needed. What you’ll do Lead and develop the recruiting team supporting Sales across the Americas, using coaching, feedback, and clear development plans to build capability and accountability. Design recruiting strategies, structured interviews, and hiring frameworks that scale across the AMER market.  Partner with Sales leaders to define talent needs, share market insights across the United States, Canada, and Latin America, and guide hiring decisions and trade-offs. Plan recruiting capacity against headcount and quota-capacity goals, balancing hiring speed, quality, and time to ramp. Embed diversity, equity, and inclusion into recruiting processes and hiring decisions. Manage a personal requisition load when needed, focusing on senior and specialized roles such as front-line managers, strategic account leaders, and technical sales talent. Use recruiting data to track team performance, identify bottlenecks, and improve hiring strategies across the Sales portfolio. Collaborate with Sales leadership, Sales Operations, Enablement, People Business Partners, Compensation, and Finance on workforce planning and consistent candidate and stakeholder experiences. What you’ll bring Experience developing recruiting teams for Sales or go-to-market organizations, delivering hiring outcomes in a scaling business across the United States, Canada, and Latin America. Ability to build trust with senior Sales leaders while staying hands-on with recruiting. Experience building scalable recruiting processes across different Sales roles and segments. Ability to use recruiting data to guide strategy, identify gaps, and explain outcomes to stakeholders. Experience sourcing, engaging, and closing passive candidates for quota-carrying, specialized, and senior Sales roles, including conversations about variable compensation and on-target earnings. Ability to navigate ambiguity, solve problems quickly, and maintain a thoughtful candidate experience. A collaborative leadership approach grounded in self-awareness, openness to feedback, and investment in team growth, with experience working remotely across time zones. A demonstrated commitment to inclusive hiring and equitable recruiting practices. Relevant experience may come from a range of professional backgrounds and transferable skills. About the team Our Sales Recruiting team is a globally distributed group of recruiters and talent acquisition professionals who partner with Sales leaders around the world. We work remote-first and asynchronously, with a focus on clear processes, honest conversations with candidates, and hiring decisions grounded in data. The team moves quickly, shares what works, and values transparency, ownership, and learning from each other while maintaining a high bar for hiring quality and candidate experience. The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity  The Solutions Engineering team are the customer facing product experts. The team enables Grafana Labs worldwide growth by educating potential and existing customers to ensure that they are happy and successful. We share our technical and product expertise with customers through demos, hands on enablement, presentations, technical evaluations and ongoing interaction. We partner closely with our Sales team to help qualify and close opportunities. The Solutions Engineering team is one of the primary routes of communication from our customers to the Product Management and Engineering teams. A Solutions Engineer is able to really listen to a prospect or customer, understand their requirements, ask the right questions to extract as much information as required and translate all that into a solution with Grafana Labs technology. They are the bridge between the highly technical engineering folks here at Grafana Labs, our customers and our Sales team. What You'll Be Doing Partnering with our Sales team to articulate the overall Grafana value proposition, vision and strategy to customers Owning the technical engagement with customers and help close complex opportunities through advanced competitive knowledge, technical skill and credibility Delivering product and technical presentations to potential and existing customers Effectively communicate with customers and internal teams to provide feedback on our products and the competitive landscape Driving product conversations based on need and problems with customers Working with the team to enhance documentation, write blog posts, record videos, contribute knowledge base articles and create other public or private enablement material What Makes you a Great Fit: 5+ years of technical pre-sales experience Be open to various and complex assignments, this will require strong judgment, collaboration, and leadership You will need first class written and oral communication skills to collaborate with our remote-first internal teams and with our worldwide customers. You will need to be able to skillfully articulate our value proposition and the technical advantages of our products You love solving technical challenges and thrive on bringing creative solutions to our customers You should have a technical mindset and a desire to grow technically.  Must be located in Sweden   Bonus Points For: Experience with Open Source technologies, or in the Metrics/Monitoring space is an advantage  Experience with sales methodologies like MEDD(P)ICC is a plus Compensation & Rewards  In Sweden, the OTE (On-Target Earnings) compensation range for this role is SEK 1,286,000 - SEK 1,544,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 100% Remote, Global Culture -  As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things. Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work. Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics. Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career. Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human. Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do. In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.  Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications

descriptionAr: About the team OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this. In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their organization. The team comprises Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals who collaborate to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible. About the role Our Federal Partnerships team brings advanced AI to the defense industrial base. You’ll own a portfolio of emerging defense technology accounts and lead their account and deal strategy. You’ll also work with the broader partnerships team to grow larger strategic relationships. You’ll independently lead customer meetings and manage your assigned emerging defense technology portfolio, working with technical teams to turn customer needs into deployed capabilities. This is a demanding, hands-on role that requires initiative, persistence, and a strong sense of responsibility for getting useful AI capabilities into customers’ hands. This role is based in Washington, DC, with up to 25% travel. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you'll: Lead account strategy and commercial execution for your emerging defense technology portfolio, from discovery and negotiation through close and expansion. Support the broader partnerships team on larger strategic relationships across the defense industrial base. Work with solutions and engineering teams to move customers from AI evaluation to deployment and sustained adoption. Maintain accurate pipeline, consumption forecasts, and clear next steps. Build trusted executive and technical relationships, connecting AI capabilities to business and mission outcomes. Anticipate customer needs and bring customer and market insights into product and partnership decisions. Coordinate across OpenAI to advance deals, remove blockers, and deliver on customer commitments. We're seeking someone with: 8+ years of combined relevant experience across government, military service, defense technology, or PaaS/SaaS businesses, including at least 2 years in private-sector, customer-facing roles. Military service and/or defense technology experience are valued. Proven private-sector results, with clear examples of business or customer outcomes you personally drove. Strong business acumen and strategic judgment, including the ability to assess opportunities, navigate stakeholders, and turn insight into action. The ability to take initiative, set priorities, and deliver results amid the ambiguity and pace of defense technology. Polished, clear communication and experience working directly with senior executives in government or the private sector. Hands-on experience applying AI tools to practical problems, with the ability to explain the approach, results, and limitations. Strong understanding of APIs and workflow integration, with the ability to engage engineering teams credibly. Initiative, urgency, and coachability, with a record of acting on feedback and following through. You might thrive in this role if you: Are customer-centric. You understand customers’ priorities and take ownership of helping them deploy useful capabilities quickly. Are deeply curious about AI. You regularly test new capabilities, explore their limits, and identify practical uses for customers. Bring a strong work ethic. You take initiative, prepare thoroughly, and follow through. You move quickly through ambiguity without sacrificing judgment or trust. Look ahead. You anticipate what customers will need next and help them identify new opportunities. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Role Overview Cohere has a strong AI narrative, the most deployable product, and a CEO who co-authored the foundational paper of modern AI. Following its recent partnership with Aleph Alpha, the company is positioned to become the transatlantic leader in sovereign AI for enterprise and government, and needs a storytelling engine to deliver that story at scale. This role sits within the team that is building that engine. In this cross functional role, you will stand up our PR and Communications function in the German market. You'll partner with the Global Corporate Communications team and EMEA Communications team to create a regional communication plan that fuels our growth among governments and enterprises in the most highly-regulated industries across DACH. You’ll nurture how we talk to customers, partners, and employees, ensuring that the corporate message resonates culturally for the German market and its audiences. This is a rare opportunity to build a comprehensive German PR function at a fast-growing company in the most dynamic space in technology. This is a role for someone who likes to take big swings – and have fun doing it – where no job is too big or too small. Key Responsibilities As the Communications Manager for Germany, you will: Own and drive Cohere’s German communications strategy, aligning corporate priorities, business objectives, product innovation, executive visibility and technical differentiation to strengthen the company’s reputation in Germany Translate Cohere’s innovations and customer success stories into compelling, locally relevant narratives for German-speaking audiences Lead proactive media engagement and newsjacking opportunities in close collaboration with EMEA Communications and EMEA Government Affairs, capitalising on relevant industry and policy developments to amplify Cohere’s voice Elevate the profile and influence of Cohere’s German leadership and spokespeople by partnering with Executive Communications to develop strategic messaging, thought leadership, media opportunities and executive visibility programmes, including for the German Country Manager. Strengthen Cohere’s reputation through customer- and partner-led storytelling, working closely with Partner Marketing to showcase German customer outcomes, deepen strategic relationships and amplify the impact of Cohere’s ecosystem in the local market. Lead and coordinate German crisis and issues communications, partnering with Corporate Communications and relevant local and regional teams to anticipate reputational risks, develop response strategies and ensure clear and timely communications. Qualifications Have 7-10 years of experience in B2B communications in DACH, or technical content, ideally in AI, enterprise software, or developer‑focused environments Have a talent for translating complex topics into different languages without losing nuance Are experienced at managing PR agencies in the German market Have experience and/or heavy interest in policy and regulatory communications, particularly within the German/EU regulatory environment Have experience running communications strategies for the DACH region Are highly organized and detail‑oriented with strong project management skills and a bias for action Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and thrive in fast‑moving, high‑growth environments Build strong cross‑functional relationships to drive clarity, consistency, and alignment across teams Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. How and Where We Work: Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. An overview of this role This position is 100% remote and will be based in the UK, Spain, and Ireland. GitLab is looking for an enthusiastic and strategic Business Development Representative (BDR) to join our growing Sales team. As a BDR at GitLab, you get the opportunity to lead the initial outreach to targeted accounts working in conjunction with the Field and Digital Marketing teams as well as the Sales and Customer Success teams. In this role you'll leverage creative marketing and sales tactics to prospect and engage with multiple buyer personas and roles to introduce GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You'll be responsible for generating qualified meetings and pipeline for GitLab's Sales organization. Our BDRs come from a diverse background. Many have worked in closing roles previously or managed teams. We have an extensive onboarding and training program at GitLab and you'll be provided with necessary DevOps and GitLab knowledge to fulfill your role. What you’ll do Execute outbound prospecting initiatives to generate qualified meetings and pipeline in your assigned territory. Generate New Logo opportunities and Growth opportunities on existing customer accounts. Conduct high-level discovery conversations with target accounts to understand business needs, qualify opportunities, and create Sales Accepted Opportunities (SAOs). Meet or exceed monthly and quarterly BDR-sourced Sales Accepted Opportunity (SAO) targets (e.g., Stage 1 and Stage 3 opportunities) by consistently converting qualified prospects into opportunities. Research and prioritize target accounts using business and industry knowledge to identify key players, uncover compelling events, and develop tailored outreach strategies. Execute a multi-touch outreach cadence (call, email, social, etc.) to all prospects in your assigned territory using Outreach to maximize engagement and conversion rates. Manage, track, and accurately report all prospecting activities and pipeline in Salesforce to provide clear visibility into performance and forecast. Collaborate with Field, Corporate, and Digital Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success teams to build targeted account lists, campaigns, and call strategies. Attend regional marketing events to engage participants, generate leads, and drive qualified Sales Accepted Opportunities (SAOs). Document and continuously improve Business Development Representative processes in the GitLab handbook in partnership with your Business Development Manager. Mentor new BDR hires to help them ramp quickly and navigate key accounts. What you’ll bring Fluency in German. Previous tech industry experience in an outbound sales development role is required. Positive and energetic phone skills, excellent listening skills, strong writing skills. Ability to prioritize tasks, manage a high volume of outreach, and consistently follow through on prospecting activities. Proven experience taking initiative, persisting through setbacks, and independently driving projects or activities through to successful outcomes. Alignment with our values and working in accordance with those values. Knowledge of business process, roles, and organizational structure. Proficiency in using Salesforce, Sales Navigator, and Outreach or similar prospecting and sequencing tools. The ability to travel for events such as trainings, team offsites, customer meetings, etc. Proficiency in English, our company language, is required for effective communication. About the team As part of GitLab's growing Sales team, you will work closely with the Field and Digital Marketing teams, as well as the Sales and Customer Success teams. Our BDRs come from diverse backgrounds, and we provide extensive onboarding and training so you have the DevOps and GitLab knowledge you need to succeed. You'll partner with Account Executives, working fully remote and distributed across multiple U.S. time zones, collaborating asynchronously through GitLab, video calls, and shared playbooks.
